verdict.rationale: Keycloak ships its own development mode (`start-dev`), which runs a throwaway local instance in Docker, and its realms act as isolated tenants. Realms can be exported and imported as JSON, so a test environment can be seeded separately from production. This is real sandbox isolation through separate instances or realms, not a dry-run mode. However, there is no dedicated hosted sandbox or test-mode feature, and community users report no supported way to test config changes and promote them to production. missing for 10: dedicated sandbox/test-mode feature, first-party test-to-production promotion workflow, independent corroboration of sandbox use for agent testing.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can test against a sandbox environment without touching production data

citations.quote: docker run -p 127.0.0.1:8080:8080 -e KC_BOOTSTRAP_ADMIN_USERNAME=admin -e KC_BOOTSTRAP_ADMIN_PASSWORD=admin quay.io/keycloak/keycloak:26.7.3 start-dev
Each realm allows an administrator to create isolated groups of applications and users.
Import and export realms as JSON files.
